title: CNN Reported Trump Used S&A Concrete for Trump Plaza
description_short: CNN reported Trump used S&A Concrete on Trump Plaza condominiums; a Second Circuit opinion described Salerno’s interest in S&A but reversed the appealing defendants’ convictions.
description_medium: CNN reported that Trump used S&A Concrete to build Trump Plaza condominiums and cited records identifying Anthony Salerno and Paul Castellano as controllers. In a related concrete-industry case, the Second Circuit recorded a jury forfeiture verdict involving Salerno’s interest in S&A, then reversed all appealing defendants’ convictions and remanded. The opinion does not mention Trump. This supports an attributed supplier relationship, not knowing participation or a RICO violation.
description_long: CNN’s July 31, 2015 account reported that Trump used S&A Concrete to build Trump Plaza condominiums and cited federal court records identifying Anthony Salerno and Paul Castellano as controllers of S&A. A Second Circuit opinion in a federal concrete-industry case described a jury forfeiture verdict awarding the government Salerno’s interest in S&A Concrete and affiliates from November 1981 through the end of 1984. The same opinion reversed all appealing defendants’ convictions and remanded for further proceedings. It does not mention Trump or Trump Plaza. Together, these sources support an attributed account of the reported supplier relationship and Salerno’s interest in the company; they do not establish that Trump knew of or joined a criminal scheme, violated RICO, or that the Trump Plaza project benefited from criminal conduct. This correction removes the frozen original’s unsupported land-price and concrete-cost figures and its conclusions of criminal participation while preserving the same reported Trump Plaza supplier event.

facts.fact: CNN reported Trump used S&A Concrete to build Trump Plaza condominiums.
CNN cited federal court records identifying Anthony Salerno and Paul Castellano as controllers of S&A.

limitations: This is an attributed news report; it does not establish Trump’s knowledge of a criminal scheme or criminal participation.

facts.fact: The Second Circuit opinion recounts the jury forfeiture verdict involving Salerno’s S&A Concrete interests from November 1981 through the end of 1984.
facts.quote: The jury further returned forfeiture verdicts against Salerno, Vincent DiNapoli, Auletta, and Halloran, awarding to the government Salerno's interests in S & A Concrete Company and its affiliates from November 1981 through the end of 1984; his interests in Glen Island Casino; and payments from Marathon Enterprises, Inc. totalling $155,000.

facts.fact: The Second Circuit reversed the appealing defendants’ convictions and remanded.
facts.quote: We therefore reverse the convictions of all appealing defendants and remand for further proceedings in the district court.

limitations: The opinion does not mention Trump or Trump Plaza and does not establish that Trump knew of or joined the concrete-industry scheme.
